newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan aluminium premiums surge on Japan trend.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan aluminium premiums surge on Japan trend.

text.p: Taking their lead from Japan, Taiwan aluminium premiums have jumped to between U$95 to $100 a tonne over London Metal Exchange cash prices compared to $84 to $89 a week earlier, traders said on Thursday.
Traders attributed the rise to anticipation of forthcoming higher third-quarter Japanese aluminium import premiums -- the benchmark for northeast Asia.
"Taiwan's aluminium premium in recent days has traded between $95 to $100 a tonne as many expect the Japanese third quarter premium to be set higher," one Taipei metal dealer told Reuters.

Japan aluminium importers this week are negotiating with foreign aluminium producers for July-September term contracts, which some traders say are likely to be set around $85 to $90 per tonne but as high as $95 a tonne over LME cash prices.
In Taiwan, aluminium premiums normally are quoted about $10 higher than Japan's, trader said.
Dealers said local trading was expected to be quite slow in coming days as long as uncertainty exists about the aluminium price trend.

In the medium to long term, local aluminium demand is expected to rise as a range of government measures to accelerate a nascent recovery in the long-dormant construction and property sectors take effect.
